questions.question: An object can be called a stationary object when:

options.text: It always moves in a straight line.
Its position does not change with time and it remains at rest.
Its motion is difficult to observe.
It is changing its position with respect to time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An object can be called a** stationary object** when it is not moving or its position is not changing with respect to its surroundings.
 
• In other words, a stationary object is at rest or in a** state of equilibrium.**
 
• This is in contrast to a moving object, which is in motion and has a changing position with respect to its surroundings.
 
• It's important to note that whether an object is stationary or not depends on the frame of reference.
 
• **For example**, an object may be stationary with respect to the ground but may be moving with respect to a moving vehicle.

questions.question: Heating ethanol with excess concentrated sulphuric acid produces:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Ethene** is produced when **ethanol **is heated with excess **concentrated sulphuric acid**, which acts as a **dehydrating agent.**
 
• The reaction takes place through an** elimination process**, where a molecule of water is removed from the **ethanol molecule, **resulting in the formation of ethene.
 
• When pure, the gas has a little **"sweet and musky"** smell and is **combustible.**
 
• It is **colorless.**
 
• The **simplest alkene** is this one.

• **Concentrated sulphuric acid** is a strong acid with the molecular formula H₂SO₄, commonly used in the chemical industry as a **dehydrating agent,** **catalyst, and electrolyte.**
 
• **Ethyne** (acetylene) is a** two-carbon alkyne **with the molecular formula C₂H₂, commonly used in the** welding and cutting industry** as a fuel gas.
 
• **Butane** is a** four-carbon alkane **with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀, commonly used as a** fuel gas in lighters, stoves, and heaters.**
 
• **Ethane** is a **two-carbon alkane** with the molecular formula C₂H₆, commonly used as a **fuel gas and refrigerant.**

questions.question: In which year did Niels Bohr propose a theory for the hydrogen atom based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities take only discrete values?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1913**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Niels Bohr:-**

 
 
• **He was a Danish physicist who made significant contributions to the development of atomic structure and quantum mechanics.**
 
• His theory for the hydrogen atom based on quantum theory is known as the Bohr model, which proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels.
 
• **In 1913 Niels Bohr proposed his theory for the hydrogen atom based on the quantum theory that some physical quantities take only discrete values.**
 
• Niels Bohr's theory proposed that electrons in an atom can only exist in certain energy levels, and when they move between levels, they emit or absorb energy in the form of photons.
 
• This theory helped to explain the spectral lines of hydrogen and paved the way for further development of quantum mechanics.

questions.question: Which of the following cells are found in the liver of mammals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kupffer cells.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kupffer cells** are found in the **liver of mammals.**
 
• Kupffer cells are **specialized macrophages** found in the liver, responsible for **removing foreign substances** such as bacteria and old red blood cells from the **bloodstream. ​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purkinje cells** are a type of **neuron **found in the **cerebellum of the brain**, involved in controlling **movement and coordination.**
 
• **Microglial cells** are immune cells found in the** central nervous system,** responsible for** maintaining brain health **and responding to** injury or infection.**
 
• **Sensory cells** are specialized cells found in the **sense organs**, such as the **eyes, ears, and nose, **responsible for **detecting stimuli **and **transmitting signals **to the brain.
 
• Therefore, option 1 (Purkinje cells), option 2 (Microglial cells), and option 4 (Sensory cells) are **incorrect **as they are not found in the liver of mammals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the magnetic lines of force?

options.text: They start from the north pole and end at the south pole.
Their relative thickness at a point gives the strength of the magnetic field at that point.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Magnetic field: The magnetic field is a field produced by the magnet. 
 
• Magnetic field lines: Magnetic fields are represented using magnetic field lines.
 
 
• It is used to visualize the strength and the direction of the magnetic field.
 
 
 
• Properties of Magnetic Field Lines
 
 
• At a point, the tangent drawn on the magnetic field line gives the direction of the magnetic field at that point.
 
• The density of the field lines gives the strength of the field. 
 
• Inside a magnet, the magnetic field lines go from the south pole to the north pole.
 
• **Outside the magnet, Magnetic field lines appear to emerge or start from the north pole and merge or terminate at the south pole.**
 
• Magnetic field lines form a closed loop.
 
• Magnetic field lines never intersect with each other.
 
• Field lines represent both magnitude and direction at any point on the field.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• The statement 3 is incorrect because the relative thickness of magnetic lines of force does not give the strength of the magnetic field.
 
• Instead, the density or closeness of the lines indicates the strength of the magnetic field at a particular point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fbd131a2f352af67bfbf2b45c34ed3054b82c4965c59431bf2c0a19bafb2d5c1.png]

questions.question: Which of the following vitamins helps to keep our skin and eyes healthy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vitamin A:**
 
• This vitamin is crucial for maintaining the health of both your skin and eyes.
 
• It is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays an essential role in ensuring normal vision.
 
• It produces pigments in the retina of the eye and promotes good vision, especially in low light.
 
• It also helps the heart, lungs, kidneys, and other organs function properly.
 
• Moreover, it is involved in the regulation of the immune system.
 
• For the skin, vitamin A helps to speed up healing, prevent breakouts, and support the skin's immune system, promoting natural moisturising.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Vitamin
 Role in Skin Health
 Role in Eye Health
 
 

 Vitamin C
 As an antioxidant, helps to protect the skin from damaging free radicals caused by UV exposure. Aids in the skin's natural regeneration process and helps prevent dry skin.
 Supports the health of blood vessels in the eye and might decrease the risk of cataracts.
 
 

 Vitamin D
 May contribute to skin health by managing the growth of cells and reducing inflammation.
 Some research points to vitamin D deficiency being associated with an increased risk of age-related macular degeneration, but its role in eye health is less established.
 
 

 
 Vitamin B (B3, B5, B7, B2, B6, B9, B12)

 

 

 

 
 
 B3 and B5 improve skin hydration, reduce redness and inflammation, and boost skin elasticity. B7 promotes healthy hair, skin, and nails. 
 B2 helps prevent cataracts. A combination of B6, B9, and B12 might reduce the risk of age-related macular degeneration.

questions.question: Which f-block element in the periodic table is represented by the Greek symbol 'alpha' and the metallic 'rays'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Actinium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Actinium:-**

 
 
• **The f-block element represented by the Greek symbol 'alpha' and the metallic 'rays' is Actinium, which has the atomic number 89 and belongs to the group 3 of the periodic table.**
 
• Actinium is a radioactive element that was discovered in 1899 by Andrundefined-Louis Debierne and named after the Greek word 'aktinos', meaning ray or beam, due to its high radioactivity.
 
• Actinium is a silvery-white metal that tarnishes in air and reacts with water and acids. It has no stable isotopes and its most stable isotope, Actinium-227, has a half-life of 21.8 years.
 
• Actinium is used in nuclear medicine for cancer treatment and as a neutron source in scientific research. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lanthanum:-**

 
 
• It is a soft, silvery-white metal that belongs to the lanthanide series and is used in the production of high-refractive-index glass, as well as in catalysts, electrodes, and other applications.
 
 
 
• **Rhenium:-**
 
 
• It is a dense, silvery-white metal that belongs to the group 7 of the periodic table and is used in high-temperature alloys, thermocouples, and catalysts.
 
 
 
• **Tungsten:-**
 
 
• It is a hard, dense, gray metal that belongs to the group 6 of the periodic table and is used in filaments, electrical contacts, and other applications.

questions.question: The respective electrical instruments which are always connected in series and are always connected in parallel are:
questions.solution:
Correct answer is **Ammeter and voltmeter**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Ammeter is used to measure the current. It is always connected in series with load to measure the quantity.

Voltmeter is used to measure the voltage. It is always connected in parallel to the load to measure the quantity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Galvanometer**

__
 
• The galvanometer is an instrument for measuring value and direction of a small electrical current or a function of the current by deflection of a moving coil.
 
• The deflection is a mechanical rotation derived from forces resulting from the current.
 
• An ammeter is also used for measuring the magnitude of the current.
 
• Galvanometer was invented by Johann Schweigger in 1820.

**Electroscope **

 
• An electroscope is an early scientific tool used to detect the presence of a body's electric charge__.
 
• Due to the Coulomb electrostatic force on it, it senses load by the movement of a test piece. On an entity, the sum of charge is proportional to its voltage.
 
• It takes hundreds or thousands of volts to generate enough charge to detect with an electroscope, so electroscopes are used with high-voltage sources such as static electricity and electrostatic machines.

questions.question: Which of the following tests is used for starch detection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine test**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **iodine test** is used for **starch detection** because iodine reacts with the starch molecules to form a blue-black color complex.
 
• The **glucose test** is used to detect the **presence of glucose** in a sample, not starch.
 
• **Starch** is a** complex carbohydrate **made up of glucose molecules.
 
• It is a common source of energy in many foods such as rice, potatoes, and bread.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** glucose test** involves the use of a reagent such as **Benedict's solution**, which changes color in the presence of reducing sugars such as glucose.
 
• The **salt test **is a test used to check the **purity of a sample** by adding salt to the sample and observing any changes in the physical properties such as solubility or melting point.
 
• The **sodium test** is a test used to detect the presence of **sodium ions **in a sample.
 
 
• It involves the use of a reagent such as , which reacts with sodium ions to form a yellow precipitate.
 
 
 
• **Starch** is an important component of many foods and is a major source of energy for humans and animals.
 
 
• It is also used in many industrial applications such as** papermaking and textile manufacturing.**

questions.question: Which of the following elements is present in an antiperspirant deodorant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Antiperspirant is a liquid/gel that is used to reduce sweating and perspiration.
 
• The Aluminium-based compounds are used because these compounds form a temporary plug within the sweat duct that stops flow of sweat.
 
• When the Aluminium comes in contact with sweat it turns into a gel that forms a plug over the sweat gland.
 
• Sweat is still produced in our body but it won't be released in the areas where antiperspirant has been applied.
 
• When an antiperspirant is applied, the salt dissolves the sweat or moisture in the underarm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnesium
 
 
• Magnesium is an abundant mineral in the human body, naturally present in many foods and available as a dietary supplement.
 
• This mineral plays a crucial role in over 300 enzyme reactions in the human body, particularly those processes that produce energy.
 
• Symptoms of magnesium deficiency can lead to paresthesias, weakness, and muscle cramping. Hypomagnesemia can also cause QT prolongation visualized on an EKG.
 
• Symptomatic hypocalcemia may require repletion of this mineral, as well as hypokalemia that is refractory to potassium repletion.
 
• Magnesium can support sports performance, mood, sleep quality, bone health, and cardiovascular health.
 
• Serum magnesium level is used for diagnosis, but it does not always correlate with intracellular magnesium level.
 
• The daily recommended dietary allowance varies by age and sex but is about 400-420 mg for men and 310-320 mg for women.
 
 
 
• Sodium
 
 
• Sodium is a chemical element with the symbol Na (from Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
 
• The melting point of sodium is 208.04 degrees Fahrenheit or 97.80 degrees Celsius.
 
• It belongs to Group 1 of the Periodic Table, making it an alkali metal, and it is present in the s-block.
 
• Sodium has a standard atomic weight of 22.990.
 
• It is a highly reactive metal and fairly abundant in the Earth's crust, typically found in salts like sodium chloride (table salt).
 
 
 
• Potassium
 
 
• ​Potassium is the seventh most abundant metal in the Earth's crust, making up about 2.4% of its total mass.
 
• The element is represented by the symbol 'K' and is the 19th element in the periodic table.
 
• It is found in various minerals within igneous rocks and is sparingly soluble.
 
• Potassium appears silvery-white and is soft enough to cut with a knife.
 
• This element is the first in the fourth row (period) in the periodic table.
 
• It has the characteristic property of tarnishing towards gray immediately upon exposure to air.
 
• Potassium is the second least dense metal, right after lithium.

questions.question: The growing voice box in boys can be seen as a protruding part of the throat called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Adam's apple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Adam's apple** is a visible protrusion in the throat caused by the thyroid cartilage, which is larger in males due to hormonal differences during puberty.
 
• The Adam's apple is not present in females or pre-pubescent males.
 
• The term "gullet" refers to the esophagus, which is the muscular tube that connects the throat to the stomach.
 
• "Corn" likely refers to the vegetable, which is not related to the topic at hand.
 
• "Adrenalin" is a hormone that is produced by the adrenal glands and is involved in the body's "fight or flight" response, but it is not related to the Adam's apple.

 [IMAGE: https://i0.wp.com/images-prod.healthline.com/hlcmsresource/images/4632-adams-apple-1296x728-body.jpg?w=1155&h=1528] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The voice box, or larynx, **is a vital organ in the body that serves a number of purposes. It is situated in the neck.
 
• The larynx is involved in breathing, producing voice, and swallowing.
 
• The vocal cords vibrate in response to air passing through them, producing sound waves in the mouth, nose, and throat.

questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transportation of water and minerals from the soil to the stems and leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem:** 

 
 
• This is the **vascular tissue** in **plants** that conducts water and dissolved nutrients upward from the root and also helps to form the woody element in the stem. 
 
• The main function of **xylem **is to **transport water,** but it also transports some nutrients through the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parenchyma:**

 
 
• This is the most common type of **plant tissue **found in the **soft parts of plants.**
 
• It is responsible for the **plant's metabolic functions, such as photosynthesis, storage of starch, fats and oils, and helps in the healing and repair of wounds.**
 
 
 
• **Collenchyma:**
 
 
• This tissue gives support to the plant and is usually found in** layers beneath the epidermis**.
 
• **Collenchyma cells** are elongated cells with thickened cell walls that provide structure and **support for the plant, particularly in regions of new growth**.
 
 
 
• **Phloem:**
 
 
• This is the** living tissue** that transports the** soluble organic compounds made during photosynthesis and known as photosynthates, in particular, sugar, from leaves to the rest of the plant where needed.**
 
• This process is called **translocation**.

questions.question: Which one of the following alloys contains a non-metal as one of its constituent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Steel **is an alloy that contains **carbon **as one of its components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brass **is an alloy made of copper and zinc, which are both metals.

 
 
• There is no non-metal present in brass.
 
 
 
• **Bronze **is an alloy of copper and tin, which are both metals.
 
 
• Like brass, bronze contains no nonmetals.
